texts.value: Histone H1 protein binds to linker DNA between nucleosomes forming the macromolecular structure known as the chromatin fiber (PubMed:33238161). Histones H1 are necessary for the condensation of nucleosome chains into higher-order structured fibers and promote formation of the H3K27me3 mark by the PRC2/EED-EZH2 complex (PubMed:33238161, PubMed:40516528)
Associates with nucleosomes, promoting condensation into higher-order structured chromatin (PubMed:33238161). Interacts with RRP1B (PubMed:19710015)
Associated with RNA polymerase II-enriched regions on chromatin (PubMed:25645921). Distributed throughout the nucleus; enriched in high-GC regions (PubMed:38530350)
Expression is activated by transcription factor CRAMP1, in collaboration with NPAT and GON4L

Citrullination at Arg-62 (H1R54ci) by PADI4 takes place within the DNA-binding site of H1 and results in its displacement from chromatin and global chromatin decondensation, thereby promoting pluripotency and stem cell maintenance
Belongs to the histone H1/H5 family
